retain: Selected round and both run identities

monitoring: Original host-stage timing, CPU/GPU telemetry and external NVML for both arms
limits: The displayed result is the maximum observed paired speedup out of five rounds, not a typical, mean or interference-free speedup.
Both selected times come from the same round. Never combine the slowest GIDS from one round with the fastest DiGiT from another.
This selection rule differs from the previous ratio of per-system minima; preserve the old three-run result separately.
Five fixed rounds, ten fresh processes: G-D / D-G / G-D / D-G / G-D. Retain all rounds, including slow or negative results, without retries.
GIDS retains default CPU scheduling; DiGiT retains original CPU2 binding. The system comparison includes this difference.
Both retain original host timing and lightweight telemetry; no perf/CUPTI, new native smoke, or model/backend changes.
